name: Snohomish
seo_title: 7 Christmas Events for Kids in Snohomish, WA 2026
seo_desc: 7 Christmas events for kids in Snohomish, WA, 3 free: Santa at Christmas at the Farm at Dairyland and more.
lede: Snohomish does Christmas the small town way: Santa arrives at the old Carnegie library for the tree lighting, then pops up in a different First Street shop each weekend while farms outside town add Santa visits and a holiday train.
celebrates: The season starts at the Snohomish Carnegie on Cedar Avenue, where the Historic Downtown Snohomish Association and the City of Snohomish hold a free tree lighting with Santa photos inside the building and a live music countdown on the plaza. On weekends Santa in the Shops moves Santa from one First Street business to the next. In December, Snohomish Winterfest fills the historic downtown with Breakfast With Santa at The Feather Ballroom, Santa in Flight sleigh videos at the Carnegie and Fire and Ice sculpting with s'mores. Out in the farm country, Dairyland hosts free Santa photos and Hidden Meadows runs Hometown Country Christmas with a train ride.
lastyear: In 2025 the Snohomish Tree Lighting took place on Saturday, November 29, from 3 to 5 pm at the Snohomish Carnegie Building. Santa arrived at 3 pm for photos inside the Carnegie, a live music Christmas countdown began on the plaza at 4:45 pm, and the tree was lit at 5 pm. The organizers asked families to bring an item downtown to help neighbors in need. That same season Hidden Meadows opened Hometown Country Christmas for the first time.
facts: Snohomish began as a settlement called Cadyville and took the name Snohomish City in 1871. It became a town in 1888 and a city in 1890, after Washington achieved statehood. The Snohomish Carnegie Building, where Santa now arrives for the tree lighting, opened in 1910 as the city's first public library with money from Andrew Carnegie. It is the oldest public building in the city and served as the library until 2003. Today Snohomish calls itself the Antique Capital of the Northwest.
trains: Snohomish has no passenger station of its own. The closest is Everett Station, served by Sounder commuter trains and by Amtrak Cascades and the Empire Builder. Close to home, Hometown Country Christmas at Hidden Meadows includes a ride on its Christmas Express train. Up US 2, the Great Northern and Cascade Railway in Skykomish gives free mini train rides in summer, and the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie runs holiday trains from its historic depot. The old Spirit of Washington dinner train operator once proposed extending its line north to Snohomish.

traditions: Santa arrives at the Snohomish Carnegie, poses for photos inside, and the city tree is lit after a live music countdown.
Santa visits a different downtown shop each weekend day, and photos with your own camera are free.
Lamb & Co. hosts a buffet breakfast with Santa and Mrs. Claus at The Feather Ballroom to benefit Make A Wish.
Families ride a green screen sleigh at the Carnegie and get a video of flying over First Street.
Dairyland on Treosti Road brings Santa in on weekends for free photos, alongside a holiday market.
kidfact: The building where Santa arrives in Snohomish was the town library for 93 years. It opened in 1910, and it is the oldest public building in the city.
faq: Where is the Snohomish tree lighting?

It takes place at the Snohomish Carnegie Building, 105 Cedar Ave, on the Saturday after Thanksgiving. Santa arrives in the afternoon for photos inside the Carnegie, a live music countdown and sing-along follows on Carnegie Plaza, and the city tree is lit at dusk. The Historic Downtown Snohomish Association runs it with the City of Snohomish, and it is free.
Where can kids see Santa in Snohomish for free?

Santa in the Shops puts Santa in a different First Street area shop on weekend afternoons in late November and December, and the visit and photo op are free with your own camera. Santa also visits Dairyland on Treosti Road on weekends, where photos with your own camera and admission are free.
Is there a Christmas train near Snohomish?

Yes. Hometown Country Christmas at Hidden Meadows on Springhetti Road includes a ride on its Christmas Express train along with a Santa visit and photo. For a real railway, the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie runs holiday trains, though its Santa trains book up early, so check availability well ahead.

Winterfest is the Historic Downtown Snohomish Association's December weekend of holiday events downtown. Recent lineups have included Breakfast With Santa at The Feather Ballroom, the Santa in Flight sleigh video at the Carnegie, and Fire and Ice, with ice sculpting teams and fire pits with s'mores kits.
Which train station is closest to Snohomish?

Everett Station is the nearest passenger rail stop for Snohomish families. Sounder commuter trains run between Everett and Seattle, and Amtrak Cascades and the Empire Builder also stop there. Snohomish itself has no passenger rail service, so families heading to Seattle holiday events by train can board in Everett.
